note: `referencePng` is exported by the Devup Bridge plugin when one serves the file, so a reference image no longer needs login or spends Figma allowance: the plugin exports the node as PNG (scale 1 with the longer edge held to 8192px like the direct path's `maxDimension`, sRGB, the node's own bounds) and the bridge hands it back as the single image block `get_screenshot` gives, through the same validation. The plugin manifest declares `enablePrivatePluginApi`, which Figma requires before it fills `figma.fileKey`; builds without it reported no key. A plugin built before this devup-mcp answers `DEVUP_BRIDGE_UNKNOWN_SCRIPT`; that read, and a reference PNG over the 8 MiB one bridge answer carries (`DEVUP_REFERENCE_PNG_TOO_LARGE`, now `DEVUP_FIGMA_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`), go to the direct path when the plugin reported the file's key, and when the direct path refuses with nothing to retry (no login) the plugin's refusal comes back with what to do instead of a login prompt. An asset too large to send says how large it was. `devup_figma_auth` no longer lists `referencePng` among what needs login. Update the plugin checkout and run the plugin again to get the new reads.
